teach.summary: In an older adult, the acutely hot knee is a tap first and a theory second.
paras: An acutely swollen knee in an older adult without trauma together with a warm knee effusion with chondrocalcinosis on radiography is the presentation that should bring calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease to the front of the differential. The underlying process is pyrophosphate crystal shedding into the joint space.

Arthrocentesis with crystal analysis and infection exclusion is the appropriate initial study. It confirms the diagnosis while separating it from septic arthritis, which shares some surface features but presents with a hot swollen knee with fever and refusal to bear weight.
Once confirmed, joint aspiration with an intra-articular or systemic anti-inflammatory is the initial management. In an older adult, the acutely hot knee is a tap first and a theory second.
teach.objective: Recognise calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease from its characteristic presentation and identify the appropriate management.
